_why: ADR 0056's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
The defect: a column named `literatureFound` whose value was
`job.result.validated`. A run on numbers a student typed in by hand
validates fine, so it exported as `literatureFound = yes` with no
citation anywhere behind it -- a manufactured provenance claim in the
tool whose whole premise is that every number traces to a source.

mutations.description: the literature column is derived from `validated` again
mutations._note: The strongest guard is the test exporting two jobs identical in literature (both zero sources) and opposite in `validated`, then asserting the two literature cells are equal. Any re-derivation from `validated` fails it, including one written by someone who has not read the ADR.

Three-state discipline. A record predating the field, or a job that errored before metadata was assembled, did not find zero sources -- nobody looked. 'Could not check' must never render as 'checked, and there was nothing'.

mutations.description: `finalValue` read from the flat path only
mutations._note: The exporter read `job.result.finalValue`; the pipeline returns it at `result.results.finalValue`. Every real job exported a blank finalValue for the life of the route, and nineteen tests agreed with the code because their fixtures were a shape production never emits.
